summary: No findings. Trust boundary is CLI argv only. parseArgs (src/playtest/cli.ts) gates every numeric value through /^[0-9]+$/ then a min/max range check (hands 1..1e9, seed 0..MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, size 3..10, button 1..size); NaN fails both comparisons, so the check fails closed. Probed live: '1e3', '0x10', '-5', 2^53, 1000000001, an ANSI-escape argument and '../../etc/passwd' as --replay-code all exit 2 with fixed text. None of these errors echoes the input, and the Options: line prints only normalised numbers or a replay code that passed validation (leading zeros come out as '5'). Values starting with '--' are rejected as missing, and repeated or unknown options are rejected. Resource use: the work is linear in --hands (capped at 1e9, which the spec allows). summarize consumes a generator, so memory is O(1) in hands. Each hand loop ends when toAct becomes null or the first rejected action breaks it. Seed word splitting (Math.floor(seed/2^32), seed>>>0) is exact for safe integers. Resolve hook (tools/playtest/resolve-ts.js): only rewrites relative extensionless specifiers to their '.ts' sibling and falls back to the original specifier. Specifiers come from the repo's own static import graph, and argv never reaches module resolution (the entry path is fixed in the npm script), so it can't be steered to load arbitrary files. package.json: the playtest script is a fixed node invocation with no shell interpolation of arguments. engines >=22.18.0 matches the local runtime (v22.18.0) and is needed because type stripping is on by default there and module.registerHooks exists. No new dependencies, no secrets, file, network or shell operations. Non-CSPRNG Xoshiro128/fnv1a32 is deliberate for reproducible playtests and does not touch the app's real deals (newReplayCode stays CSPRNG).
